name: Tractor Supply
key_signal: TSCO has cratered ~40% over the past six months to trade just above its 52-week low near $30, sitting far below its 200-day SMA ($45) even as short-term momentum (mom_21d +1.6%, MACD histogram turning positive) hints at stabilization.
thesis: After a brutal 32%/40% drawdown over 63/126 days, TSCO now trades at just 13.7x forward earnings with a 45.5% ROE, 36% gross margins, and a 3.15% dividend yield — valuation metrics that look cheap relative to its historical premium specialty-retail multiple. The 27-analyst consensus remains 'buy,' RSI at 46 shows the stock is no longer oversold but not stretched either, and the recent positive MACD histogram alongside a modest 21-day momentum uptick suggests the selling pressure that drove the stock from the low-60s to the low-30s may be exhausting itself, setting up a mean-reversion trade back toward the 50-day SMA (~$30.57) and beyond.
bear_case: The technical trend remains decisively bearish — price is below both the 50-day and 200-day moving averages with no golden cross, and earnings growth is already negative (-8.1%) even before any further deterioration in discretionary rural spending; more concerning, debt-to-equity of ~255% leaves TSCO with a leveraged balance sheet just as revenue growth has slowed to 3.6%, meaning further margin compression or a consumer pullback could pressure the dividend and compound the de-rating that already wiped out over a third of the market cap, and the 40% 6-month decline may reflect a structural deterioration (competitive/tariff/traffic issues) rather than a temporary overreaction, in which case the 'cheap' 13.7x forward multiple is a value trap.
